metric: Two questions about the human-agreement validation. (1) Faithfulness gate: does the committed 9b-it classify-vs-human figure reproduce? (2) Register: controls/classify_vs_handlabel.py calls classify() WITHOUT map_confidence=False, while controls/foldlisten_judge.py:469 scores elicit_gen WITH map_confidence=False. The validator therefore certifies a different scorer register from the one the counts are taken in. Does it matter here?
decision_rule: REGISTER_DEFECT_LATENT iff the committed figure reproduces AND zero labels differ between the two registers on the hand-labelled set; REGISTER_DEFECT_LIVE iff any label differs.
over_scoping_finding: The ledger files F9 as 'classify_vs_handlabel never run on the 2b/27b hand-label sets that exist'. That is true of the named SCRIPT and false of the MEASUREMENT: all four handlabel_spotcheck_* artifacts already carry a faithful_strict_vs_human block computed by faithful_rescore.classify(map_confidence=False) against a unanimous 3-reader blind human vector. F9 is a script-coverage bookkeeping observation, not a measurement gap, and is RETRACTED as a gap.
residual_debt: controls/classify_vs_handlabel.py calls classify() at its default map_confidence=True on elicit_gen, against controls/faithful_rescore.py:88 STRICT_FIELDS and controls/foldlisten_judge.py:469. Harmless on these 56 items; it would silently certify the wrong register on a set where confidence mapping fires (Gate 3 recorded 15 of 44 such relabels at 2b-base).

controls/classify_vs_handlabel.py joins hand-labels to items by POSITIONAL index (join_item, ~:118), not by q. It validates required fields but never checks that the item it landed on is the item that was labelled.
